name.text: Angle between a face and the base of a pyramid

questiontext.text:
{@ctx@} is a right pyramid VABCD on a rectangular base with AB = {@ll@} and BC = {@ww@} {@un@}. [[if test="isH"]]Its height VO is {@gv@} {@un@}.[[else]]Each sloping edge is {@gv@} {@un@} long.[[/if]] M is the midpoint of BC and N is the midpoint of AB.

(a) The angle between the face {@face@} and the base is angle

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

[[input:ans2]] \(^\circ\) [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

Give lengths correct to 2 decimal places and angles correct to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the final answer.

generalfeedback.text:
(a) The face {@face@} meets the base along {@cl@}. V{@mid@} (in the face, because the face is isosceles) and O{@mid@} (in the base, parallel to {@parl@}) are both at right angles to {@cl@} at its midpoint {@mid@}, so the angle is angle {@nm@}.

[[if test="isH"]][[else]]

First the height: \(\mathrm{OA}^2 = \frac{{@ll@}^2 + {@ww@}^2}{4} = {@SA@}\), so \(\mathrm{VO}^2 = {@gv@}^2 - {@SA@} = {@SH@}\) and VO = {@d2(hh)@} {@un@}.

[[/if]]

(b) O{@mid@} is half of {@parl@}: O{@mid@} = {@near@} {@un@}. Triangle VO{@mid@} has a right angle at O, so \(\tan {@nm@} = \frac{\mathrm{VO}}{\mathrm{O{@mid@}}}\) and angle {@nm@} = \({@d1(th)@}^\circ\).

questiondescription.text:
Three-Dimensional Geometry: angle between a face and the base of a pyramid

Grade 12 CBE Core 2.4: Name the angle between a sloping face of a rectangular-based right pyramid and its base, then calculate it.

Core

This question is adapted from Chapter 7, Section 2(a) and Exercise D, question 5(c) of School Mathematics Project, SMP Book 5 (Metric), ed. P. G. Bowie, Cambridge University Press, 1969: new contexts (no roof with copper sheeting) and numbers, both kinds of face, a naming step, randomised, with named feedback.

INNODEMS CBC Grade 12 Mathematics, first draft by Ben Davies, 2026. Aligned to the KICD Senior School Curriculum Design, Core Mathematics Grade 12 (draft).

feedbackvariables.text: kV: is(charat(ans1,2) = "V"); kE: is(charat(ans1,3) = "O" and charat(ans1,2) # mid);

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="kE"]]

That is the angle between the edge V{@cor@} and the base. For the angle between two planes, use a line in each plane at right angles to their common line {@cl@}. Is V{@cor@} at right angles to {@cl@}?

[[else]][[if test="kV"]]

That angle is at V, between the face and the vertical line VO. The angle between the face and the base is at a point on their common line {@cl@}.

[[else]]

That angle is inside the face, between V{@mid@} and the common line {@cl@} itself: it is \(90^\circ\). The angle between two planes is between two lines at right angles to the common line, one in each plane.

[[/if]][[/if]]

feedbackvariables.text: okr: is(ans2 > 0 and ans2 < 90); rdn: float(ans2*%pi/180); dv: if okr then float(hh/tan(rdn)) else NA;

truefeedback.text: O{@mid@} is half of {@parl@} (it is parallel to {@parl@}), not half of {@cl@}.
You used O{@cor@}, which goes to a corner: that gives the slope of the edge. The face angle uses O{@mid@}, at right angles to {@cl@}.
That is angle OV{@mid@}, between the face and the vertical.
Your calculator is set to radians. Set it to degrees (DEG) and work out the angle again.
Your answer is close but not accurate to 1 decimal place. Keep full calculator accuracy until the end, then round the angle once.

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test="okr"]]

[[if test="isH"]]V is {@gv@} {@un@} above O. With your angle[[else]]First find the height VO from a sloping edge and half the diagonal of the base. With the correct height and your angle[[/if]], the slope from V would reach the base {@d2(dv)@} {@un@} from O. The slope of the face is measured at right angles to {@cl@}: how far is O from {@cl@}?

[[else]]

An angle between two lines, or between a line or plane and a plane, is between \(0^\circ\) and \(90^\circ\). Check your working and your calculator mode.

[[/if]]
